code:
grep "ERROR" agent.log | wc -l

# grep searches agent.log for lines containing "ERROR" and passes them to wc

# wc -l counts the number of lines received; result is the total error count

ls -la | sort -k5 -n | tail -3

# ls -la lists files with details; sort -k5 -n sorts by the 5th column (file size) numerically

# tail -3 keeps only the last 3 lines; result is the three largest files

cat results.csv | grep "fail" | head -10

# cat prints results.csv; grep keeps only lines containing "fail"

# head -10 keeps only the first 10 of those; result is the first ten failures
description: These pipelines connect search, counting, sorting, and filtering commands with pipes.

steps.description: grep selects lines containing ERROR from agent.log, and wc -l counts those selected lines.

steps.answer: The pipeline keeps the three largest files from the listing.
steps.question: Which files remain after sorting the detailed listing by size and keeping the last three lines?

steps.description: ls -la produces detailed rows. sort uses the numeric fifth column, and tail keeps the final three rows.
cat sends results.csv to grep, which keeps lines containing fail. head then keeps the first ten of those lines.

title: Compose shell pipelines
